class.name: CrashReports
class.brief_description: Reports of runs of the game that crashed or were closed by force.
class.description: Each run of the game leaves a note in [code]user://crashes[/code] saying what it runs on, and removes it when it ends cleanly. When the game next starts, a note left behind is a run that crashed, was closed by force, or lost power: a report of it is written beside it, as a text file the player can read and send. It has the engine and game versions, the OS, processor, memory and GPU, anything the game added with [method set_context], and the end of that run's log, where a crash's backtrace is. Nothing leaves the device until the player agrees. With Purr's online services, the option [code]privacy/send_crash_reports[/code] in [Options] is their answer: while it's on, every report waiting is sent once they're signed in, and removed from the device once the service has it. Before a report is sent, the player's home folder becomes [code]~[/code], and anything shaped like an email or IP address is removed. A report longer than the service takes (64 KiB) is sent with its start and as much of the end of its log as fits. A game can also tell the player after a crash, show the report, or offer to send it: [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: if CrashReports.previous_run_crashed(): $CrashDialog.show_report(CrashReports.get_reports()[0]) [/codeblock] Runs started from the editor aren't watched: stopping one kills it, which would read as a crash every time. The newest 20 reports are kept. Turn it off with [code]crash_reports/enabled[/code] in Project Settings.

method.name: delete_report
method.description: Deletes a report, given its path from [method get_reports]: once the player has sent it, say.

method.name: get_context
method.description: What the game has added with [method set_context].

method.name: get_reports
method.description: The paths of the reports kept, newest first. Each is a text file to read with [FileAccess].

method.name: previous_run_crashed
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the run before this one didn't end cleanly, and its report is the newest in [method get_reports].

method.name: send
method.description: Sends a report, given its path from [method get_reports], to the game's online service, and returns a signal to await. Its result is a [Dictionary] with [code]ok[/code], and on failure [code]error[/code] and [code]message[/code]. Once the service has the report, it's removed from the device, as it is when the service refuses it as malformed (it never would take it). Send one only when the player has agreed to it: when [code]privacy/send_crash_reports[/code] is on, Purr sends them all itself. [codeblock] var result: Dictionary = await CrashReports.send(CrashReports.get_reports()[0]) [/codeblock]

method.name: set_context
method.description: Adds something about this run to its report, should it crash: the level being played, the save loaded, the graphics settings. [code]null[/code] removes it.
